Meanwhile, we will continue to explore the application of technological solutions to assist banks in identifying, measuring, and monitoring their climate risk exposures; one example is the upcoming launch of a cloud-based platform to facilitate banks’ physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional competence of practitioners, we will also develop the Professional Level module on “Green and Sustainable Finance” under the “Enhanced Competency Framework” for banking professionals in 2024. Hong Kong is well-positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfill this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposal in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope of the “Government Green Bond Programme” to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market; simultaneously, through the “Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme,” we aim to attract more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions, and corporations to raise green capital through Hong Kong, and explore potential synergies between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to assist in implementing the Government-funded “Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme” to expand the talent pool for green finance in Hong Kong. As Co-Chair of the “Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group” (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives aimed at promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Steering Group will focus on three key areas in 2024: sustainability disclosure, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another key priority, through the “Alliance for Green Commercial Banks,” the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various dedicated initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market insights, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to help financial institutions establish their distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our collaboration with the “Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero,” the “Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance,” and the “Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership.” As a responsible investor, the HKMA has committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or sooner. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring portfolio resilience throughout the journey towards net zero. Recognizing that achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement requires an economy-wide transition, we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus on assets that can deliver positive climate outcomes for the real economy, while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. As an environmentally responsible organization, the HKMA’s decarbonization strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest developments in markets, regulation, technology, and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the HKMA’s climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of leveraging technological solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. Moreover, we will continue to actively encourage staff participation in our sustainability efforts, including launching promotional campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and streamlining office processes and practices. Additionally, the HKMA will continue to uphold consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement practices, including evaluating suppliers’ ESG practices during selection and contract renewal. Building upon the Green Data Centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to adhering to designated certification standards. Regarding regular upgrades to data centre facilities, we will incorporate green design and operational practices alongside keeping pace with the latest technological advancements. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and proactively modernize internal systems to improve efficiency and minimize potential risks wherever possible. Finally, regarding social focus areas, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, and raise public awareness of financial fraud prevention.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable organization, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the broader Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its sustainability-related strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of relevant initiatives; and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations and practices. In pursuit of sound institutional governance, the HKMA has put in place a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and establishes effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability efforts. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability efforts, and provide recommendations; the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides leadership at the management level on the HKMA’s overall Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) strategy and policy; regarding responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within that office; and for other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups are tasked with planning and implementing sustainability measures related to banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (CASG), co-established by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates efforts among financial regulators, government bureaux and departments, industry participants, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the HKMA’s sustainability initiatives over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new centralized platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability-related work across different functional areas of the HKMA1. The Steering Committee provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans concerning ESG-related matters across four functional areas: banking, market development, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by various departments of the HKMA; assesses the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees external communication strategies. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Steering Committee includes the three Deputy Chief Executives as standing members. In addition, Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainability matters will be invited to attend meetings of the Steering Committee to report on key achievements and future plans relating to their respective portfolios. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups from the Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office of the HKMA. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA co-established the CASG2 with the SFC in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the CASG provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the CASG, please refer to the chapter entitled "Strengthening the Development of a Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change poses a significant risk to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong’s financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals as well as the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily business operations. To continue performing their vital functions within the financial system and to channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to address and manage climate risks, and on accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The HKMA is committed to formulating various policy measures to enhance the banking sector’s resilience to climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the economy's transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of this circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey of selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices regarding transition planning with the industry, and will organize seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experiences among industry participants. Regarding disclosure requirements, in light of the latest international developments—including the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Sustainability Disclosure Standards released in June, and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s (Basel Committee) consultation launched in November on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks—the HKMA is stepping up its efforts to refine the sustainability-related disclosure framework for banks in Hong Kong. Specifically, the HKMA is working with local relevant authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for adopting the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards in Hong Kong. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and provided guidance to help banks further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Significant progress has been made in implementing the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the bank supervisory process. Climate risk management has now been included as a standing agenda item in prudential meetings held with bank management. Bank supervisors have also adopted an enhanced CAMEL rating system1 that incorporates climate risk factors to assess banks’ risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the bank supervisory process, the HKMA revised its “Green” assessment framework to focus on banks’ transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the Supervisory Review Process, which is used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address climate risks. Key priorities under the 2023 two-year plan: Following the conclusion of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management,” the HKMA launched a round of thematic examinations on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. These thematic examinations covered four key areas: governance structure for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and organizational culture, awareness, and communication. The HKMA made several enhancements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of concurrent economic and climate change shocks. Following these enhancements, and as part of the HKMA’s regular supervisor-led stress testing program, the second round of climate risk stress testing was launched in June to conduct a comprehensive assessment of banks’ climate risk exposures and to further enhance their capacity to manage climate risks. A total of 44 banks participated in this stress test, representing an increase of over 60% compared to the initial pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also organized a Climate Risk Stress Testing Forum in November, which attracted as many as 300 banking professionals. By facilitating the sharing of experiences among banks, this event helped deepen the industry’s overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultative meetings to review banks’ progress in implementing the HKMA’s Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management.” The HKMA met with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks along with other publicly available information to assess their progress. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA’s supervisory expectations. With growing global attention to climate change and concerted efforts to address it, the HKMA has observed increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, and some banks have offered such products to meet customer needs. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks’ sale of green and sustainable investment products and issued a circular in November, setting out the standards expected by the HKMA and sharing observed good practices. This circular covers multiple areas, including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and record-keeping, aiming to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of related investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For instance, technology can improve data availability and risk analytics, enhancing banks’ ability to manage climate risks. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot version of a cloud-based platform to enable banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. Furthermore, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technological solutions can assist in physical risk assessments. Separately, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable approaches to anti-money laundering (AML) through the use of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, thereby reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online common data submission platform to fully automate the collection of financial crime risk data, thereby streamlining banks’ processes for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA organized the “Green Fintech Competition,” aiming to identify market-ready solutions to help the banking sector address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 submissions from approximately 70 companies. In December, the HKMA hosted the “Green and Sustainable Banking Symposium,” providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the role of low-carbon technologies and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and the Mainland, and to announce the results of the “Green Fintech Competition.” The event attracted around 400 participants from banks, technology firms, regulators, and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and promote greater consistency in green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA developed a local green taxonomy framework with the assistance of consultants. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the “Prototype Hong Kong Green Taxonomy,” seeking stakeholder views on the establishment and implementation of a green taxonomy. Based on the feedback received, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying additional areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has identified environmental crime as a predicate offense for money laundering. Given the nexus between AML and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues, this area is receiving increasing attention from regulators. Recognizing that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to enhance its current surveillance efforts. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in various Financial Stability Reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA contributes to further enriching climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s Transition Planning Working Group, the HKMA participates in analyzing the interplay between transition planning by financial and non-financial corporations and financial stability, enabling policymakers to adopt forward-looking and dynamic perspectives on climate-related financial risks. On the research front, the HKMA undertook several applied research projects examining the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. Research topics included climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG fund flows3, the impact of climate change on property prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance across global supply chains5. The findings from these studies have enhanced the HKMA’s understanding of the implications of climate change and ESG issues for financial stability, informing relevant policy formulation. Domestically, this research supports the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA shares its research findings with a wide range of stakeholders through international events on climate-related matters and various channels such as the HKMA Research Memorandum. The HKMA’s Liquidity Facilities Framework is a secured backstop funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. In line with NGFS recommendations, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such engagement, the HKMA helps foster international and regional policy dialogue on tackling climate change and its implications for financial stability, while drawing insights to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading regional green and sustainable finance hub, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the financial sector’s response to climate and environmental risks, accelerates the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supports the Government’s climate strategies. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing sustainable finance opportunities, with key work areas covering sustainability disclosure, ecosystem building, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainability Disclosure Working Group was established to formulate a roadmap for the adoption of IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards in Hong Kong. The roadmap will cover four key areas: sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Task Force was also set up to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group has also strengthened the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. In particular on the data front, we continued to promote the use of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies, launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong’s status as a regional and global green and sustainable finance hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to capture investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To facilitate skills training in the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government’s “Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme”, which provides subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates undertaking relevant training and obtaining relevant qualifications in green and sustainable finance. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications had been registered as eligible under the scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications had been approved. The HKMA also launched a new module on “Green and Sustainable Finance” at the Foundation Level under the Banking Professional Qualification Framework. This module aims to foster talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking sector to develop the Professional Level of this module to meet the rapidly growing demand for professionals in green and sustainable finance. To help financial institutions and corporates, especially SMEs, better understand key climate and sustainability-related topics—including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions accounting, and transition planning—the HKMA collaborated during the year with relevant government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), to organise a series of seminars and thematic workshops, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. On the student front, following the launch of the “Sustainable Finance Internship Programme” in 2022, training sessions were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns’ and university undergraduates’ understanding of sustainable finance. Recognising the potential of technology in bridging climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, the HKMA is committed to making relevant data more accessible and enhancing its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancements to provide a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, corporates, and the public. Key enhancements include an electronic platform for sustainability disclosure, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, as well as more centralised, user-friendly, and searchable data and resources. During “Hong Kong Green Week”, the Steering Group also co-organised the “Leveraging Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance” event with Cyberport and InvestHK, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong’s strengths in green technology. “Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme” was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia, and advisory firms. The flagship event of “Hong Kong Green Week” was the “Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum”, co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together over 400 guests, including top decision-makers from the global business and financial communities, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industry, circular economy, future development of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in emerging and developing markets in the Asia-Pacific region. The forum received strong support from both public and private sectors, with over 10 roundtables, seminars, and other networking events co-organised. Topics covered included climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition finance, green finance taxonomy, and financing for green development in Belt and Road regions. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-hosted the “Asia Climate Finance Roundtable” on 29 February 2024 to discuss key measures for scaling up climate finance and the role of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These events form part of the HKMA’s broader efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms for participants to drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting regional green and sustainable finance development. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the “Alliance for Green Commercial Banks” as a collaborative platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutes, and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has organised 22 training sessions and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from across the globe, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, together with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second cutting-edge research report titled “Developing Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategies: Case Studies”. During the year, the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established “Coalition for Sustainable Investment Capacity Building” (CASI) and the “Green Investment and Finance Partnership” (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Green Development International Alliance. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong chapter to support net-zero efforts by financial institutions in Hong Kong and the Mainland. The HKMA serves in an advisory capacity to support GFANZ’s work. To demonstrate the Government’s commitment to tackling climate change, promoting green finance, and striving to make Hong Kong a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the “Government Green Bond Programme” in 2018. The HKMA assists in issuing green bonds under the programme. To date, the Government has issued approximately US$25 billion equivalent in green institutional and retail bonds, with proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the programme, the Government publishes an annual “Green Bond Report”, detailing the allocation of proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. In the 2023-24 fiscal year, the Government continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds, issuing approximately US$6 billion equivalent in green bonds in June. This triple-tranche issuance covered bonds of different tenors in US dollars, euros, and renminbi, attracting a diverse range of investors and receiving an enthusiastic response, with subscriptions reaching nearly US$30 billion equivalent. Notably, the issuance size of renminbi bonds increased from RMB 10 billion in January to RMB 15 billion, and a 10-year renminbi bond was introduced for the first time, helping to extend the Government’s renminbi yield curve and further enrich offshore renminbi product offerings. The strong response from global investors to the Government’s green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued a second batch of green retail bonds totalling HK$20 billion to further promote market development and advance financial inclusion. This issuance provided the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, enabling them to participate in and benefit from Hong Kong’s green finance development.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) plays a pivotal role in promoting green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, it has led the way in green and sustainable asset investment by requiring its external investment managers to proactively exercise ownership rights and integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into the management of the Exchange Fund’s investments. Adhering to the principle of "Capital Preservation First, Long-term Enhancement Second,"¹ the HKMA invests prudently, believing that adequate attention to ESG factors helps mitigate relevant investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a "Net Zero by 2050" target² for its "Investment Portfolio," the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment journey with an emphasis on sustainability—particularly the pressing issue of climate change—to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieve better risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial sector and the central banking community. Through stewardship and collaborative initiatives, the HKMA strives to foster a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. Figure 1: The Exchange Fund’s Responsible Investment Journey Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is essential for integrating sustainability and planning credible climate transitions to achieve net-zero targets. In fulfilling its commitment to support the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration³ and the Strategic Plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example. In accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), this chapter has been prepared to report on the responsible investment of the Exchange Fund. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC), chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in managing the Exchange Fund’s investments. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practice responsible investment while safeguarding the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under EFAC, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the EFIO. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and oversees various ESG initiatives within the EFIO. Motions and progress discussed at quarterly meetings of the ESG Committee are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the EFIO. Furthermore, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the EFIO, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the EFIO, to realize the HKMA’s overall ESG goals. Figure 2: Responsible Investment Governance Structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office As illustrated in Figure 1, the EFIO embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainable development has evolved rapidly, moving beyond risk considerations to become a strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the EFIO has revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone when the EFIO established a new Business Strategy Department led by the Chief Strategy Officer to coordinate and lead strategic development, incorporating the former Responsible Investment Team—now renamed the Sustainable Investment Team—which previously belonged to the Risk Management and Compliance Division. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA’s shift from a risk-based focus to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related matters in investment. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the EFIO on integrating ESG factors and assists senior management in managing ESG risks and opportunities, particularly those related to climate change, across different types of investments: Public Market Investments — The Credit, Regulation, and Oversight Committee, composed of senior executives of the EFIO, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models based on input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of fixed-income portfolios through regular reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Division. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios from an ESG perspective (see the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 40). Private Market Investments — The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal. The HKMA recognizes that physical and transition risks⁴ arising from climate change, as well as related opportunities, will impact the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The United Nations Environment Programme’s Emissions Gap Report 2023⁵ projects that unless greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced globally, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels before 2030. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological development, or behavioral changes to curb rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded assets. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events pose additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund; therefore, it places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund’s "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach with a clear focus on decarbonization and transition. The following sections detail these approaches. Figure 3: The HKMA’s Three-Pronged Approach to Responsible Investment In pursuing its net-zero goal, the HKMA favors active engagement over exclusion or divestment from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Outright exclusion of certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risk profiles. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition—including those in high-emission sectors—that possess superior technology and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not solve carbon emission problems. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and exercising active ownership, the HKMA supports these industries in transitioning toward sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby driving positive change both for the industries themselves and for the world at large. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategy to adopt a comprehensive approach aimed at achieving transition outcomes aligned with both the Exchange Fund’s and global net-zero targets, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to facilitate climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolio (Figure 4). The HKMA’s responsible investment maintained strong momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new actively managed global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition, managed by external investment managers, and expanded the use of customized low-carbon equity indices to another externally managed portfolio. Moreover, green, social, and sustainability bonds prioritized for investment outperformed their benchmarks, demonstrating the concept of "doing good while doing well." In private markets, the HKMA actively built a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic trends such as climate and energy transitions. For instance, during the year, the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition funds, underscoring its commitment to addressing Asia’s climate transition needs. Figure 4: Continued Implementation of Measures to Promote ESG Investing The HKMA has invested in a company specializing in producing eco-friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic matter such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature environments to produce plastics, this company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. Made entirely from waste, this plastic material serves as a substitute for oil-based resins commonly used in retail, consumer durables, and other industries, offering a sustainable and versatile alternative. It is also compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is firmly committed to supporting the circular economy. The diagram below illustrates the positive environmental outcomes resulting from its advanced plastic production process: Managed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) is an innovative initiative that combines institutional investors’ capital with IFC’s own funds to scale up sustainable financing for private sector companies in emerging markets. The HKMA committed US$1 billion each in two tranches to MCPP in 2017 and 2019 respectively, and further collaborated with the IFC to launch a new global climate-related investment platform, "MCPP One Planet," in 2021—the world’s first Paris Agreement-aligned cross-sectoral emerging market loan portfolio. Through the MCPP, the HKMA has committed loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate, and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The IFC has collected data on MCPP loans. According to IFC reports, the HKMA’s loan commitments have supported emerging markets and developing countries in areas such as economic transformation and human resource development. Specifically, projects financed by the HKMA are projected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent annually, equivalent to the emissions generated by an average gasoline-powered car traveling 14 billion miles. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and build industry capacity.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organisation, adopting a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA places great emphasis on staff well-being and social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA has set sustainability targets under three pillars: Environment, People, and Community. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee)1, established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the primary decision-making body for various organisational sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee was formerly known as the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, and is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategy, and policies on organisational sustainability and corporate social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and submits regular progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Team provide support in coordinating the organisation's sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and discussing ways to create a green workplace, while the latter aims to foster a culture of volunteerism. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transition. Key areas of focus include implementing decarbonisation strategies in its daily operations, such as operating green buildings and data centres, practising green commuting, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools, and greener working practices, reducing waste, and building a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to employ carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and adopt carbon offsetting measures for emissions that are difficult to abate. Beyond the above-mentioned environmental commitments regarding its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce greener operational solutions for the wider community, ranging from channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communications, to electronic payment and coin collection programmes for the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capacity, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and prioritises staff well-being. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages staff participation in volunteer and charitable activities; considers social enterprises in its procurement; promotes consumer education on financial services; and collaborates with the banking sector to ensure fair access to basic banking services for all sectors of society. The remainder of this chapter sets out the details of the aforementioned strategies. Under the HKMA’s overall Enterprise Risk Management framework, the Risk Committee2, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as increased flooding or other damage caused by extreme weather events, may affect the HKMA’s offices and hinder staff commuting. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its Business Continuity Plan to cope with extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure staff are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. The design of the offices also incorporates various measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA’s energy use, air travel, and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA’s climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) in all aspects of its organisational operations by 2050 or sooner. As a near-term emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting its entire existing vehicle fleet to electric vehicles; and using 2015 as the base year, to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or sooner through various decarbonisation and offsetting strategies. Despite challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will adopt a multi-pronged approach, as far as practicable, to minimise Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions (e.g., paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel). The HKMA’s long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were established with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which has also been validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste data disclosed in this report6. The scope and criteria of the verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the 2022 Annual Report, the HKMA published its inaugural standalone 2022 Sustainability Report. The HKMA’s enhanced ESG reporting efforts have been recognised, receiving an ESG Award in the "Public Sector/Not-for-Profit Organisations" category at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulator to receive an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for meeting high ESG standards, noting that the Sustainability Report is clear and readable, and that the appointment of an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to transparent and accountable reporting. Furthermore, the HKMA received the top Gold Award in the "Non-profit and Charitable Organisations" category at the Hong Kong Management Association's "2023 Best Annual Report Awards". The judging panel praised the HKMA’s Annual Report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making effective use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA’s determination to enhance financial literacy and promote financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA’s dedication to caring for the environment, its staff, and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has presented the HKMA with the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impact of its operations. Its internal Green Office Guidelines provide guidance to staff on resource usage and office waste generation. The HKMA has integrated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of both owned and leased premises. When renovating offices, existing furniture and fitting materials are reused wherever possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly construction and decoration materials are given priority. Adhering consistently to these practices, the HKMA was awarded LEED7 Gold certification and BEAM Plus Interiors8 Gold rating in 2021 and 2022 respectively for parts of its offices renovated at Two International Finance Centre. Adopting new technologies and leveraging existing ones to improve energy efficiency remains a key focus for the HKMA. In addition to promoting good habits, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of LED lighting, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimising energy use in IT network infrastructure. The HKMA’s energy consumption has continued to decrease, reaching 2.59 MWh per capita9 in 2023, representing a 29.7% reduction from the 2015 baseline (Chart 1). Given the nature of the HKMA’s daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions primarily stem from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO2e10 per capita, a decrease of 45.2% compared to 2015 (Chart 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies, automated and streamlined workflows, built a digital workplace, and enhanced online collaboration within the organisation.11 Paperless meetings have become the primary mode of meetings at the HKMA. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, various internal administrative tasks are mainly handled through electronic processes. Moreover, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digital working modes, replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. Meanwhile, the implementation of an electronic recordkeeping system is underway. These green and digital initiatives have yielded positive results. The HKMA’s paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per capita, a significant reduction of 64.8% compared to 2015 (Chart 3). Following the post-pandemic resumption of most international events to in-person formats, and the need to promote the development of Hong Kong’s status as an international financial centre, it has inevitably become necessary for HKMA staff to undertake overseas business trips. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff attending overseas events to take direct flights or combine different business trips where feasible. At the organisational level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO2e in 2023 through the purchase of Sustainable Aviation Fuel. Additionally, the HKMA participated in a Gold Standard12 certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this programme supports waste-to-energy projects, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA’s procurement process takes sustainability and environmental factors into account. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation’s procurement policies and procedures, the existing practice of procuring green products has been formalised, adhering to the environmental specifications of the Government’s "Green Procurement List", particularly for electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, ESG factors and innovative proposals that enhance productivity and efficiency have been incorporated into tender evaluation criteria. At the same time, all suppliers are required to commit to complying with environmental regulations. Following the "4R" principles—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Details of non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, are provided in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA directly participated for the first time in the Lai See Recycling Programme organised by the property management company of the International Finance Centre. Staff collected approximately 3,000 used but intact lai see envelopes. These envelopes were subsequently handed over to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for reuse during the following Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA’s operations and backup data centres account for a major portion of the organisation’s total energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for Existing Data Centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)13. In 2023, based on the assessment guidelines "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" issued in 2021, the HKMA’s two data centres were awarded "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to receive these ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centres has always been a key focus of the Technology Division. To this end, the division adopted green designs during renovation works and implemented energy-efficient best practices to lower PUE and achieve relevant targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the data centres' environmental facilities and continuous optimisation of environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. With the Technology Division continuously improving the energy utilisation of the data centres, the HKMA commissioned an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green performance of the data centres and formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in various aspects. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the completion of the study, the HKMA began preparations to obtain the "Green Data Centre" certification under the BEAM Plus scheme. The certification process is highly comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the Technology Division implemented optimisation measures based on the consultant's recommendations to enhance energy performance as well as health-related elements of the working environment within the data centres.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has conducted an independent verification of the 2023 Environmental Data (the “2023 Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The 2023 Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste disposed of at landfills and recyclable waste), their respective intensities, and changes compared to the 2015 baseline. In addition, the 2023 Data includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and changes compared to the level when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste). The verification scope covers a total of five office and warehouse assets, comprising four offices located at: 1) Two International Finance Centre; 2) Hopewell Centre; 3) One Pacific Place; 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre; and a warehouse located at 5) Lok Sing Industrial Centre, Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the five assets. This verification engagement was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to obtain a reasonable level of assurance for forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of data by tracing selected sample data back to its source, reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and performed reliability testing. The verification process also included validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and examining selected representative data and information. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the data. Our verification work was conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data is materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record, and the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached new record highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current climate change mitigation measures. As we address global warming, the materialization of climate-related risks is set to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Furthermore, heightened geopolitical tensions, an increasingly fragmented global economic landscape, growing concerns over energy security, and uncertain economic prospects all pose greater challenges for countries in tackling climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Globally, Asia faces the most severe transition challenges. As noted by the World Economic Forum, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a pivotal role in determining whether the world can successfully achieve its net-zero emissions targets. As Asia's leading international financial centre, Hong Kong must strengthen its leadership role and fully leverage the power of finance to support and drive the regional transition. To this end, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) published the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, outlining our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating sustainability principles into the core of the financial system. Our efforts focus on enhancing the financial sector's capacity to manage climate-related risks on one hand, and assisting the industry in seizing emerging opportunities on the other. At the same time, we are leading by example. The HKMA’s sustainability work encompasses four key areas: supporting the banking sector in achieving net zero, investing in a sustainable future, facilitating net-zero financing, and promoting more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a critical role in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and Asia, yet banks themselves face significant risks during this process. Under the Action Plan, we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive for net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or sooner, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or sooner. We also require all banks to enhance disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuously strengthening banks' climate risk management capabilities, we also provide guidance on transition planning to help them build resilience and better manage associated risks. We are also working with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong’s sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, aiming to further improve transparency in related activities. Additionally, we are refining the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched last May to include more sustainable activities, including transition activities. By providing clear criteria, we aim to channel more capital toward sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change poses significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. However, it also presents opportunities for growth and positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainability outcomes can be aligned without conflict. Accordingly, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s Investment Portfolio by 2050 or sooner, and have pledged under the Action Plan to support Asia’s climate transition through the Fund’s investments. Currently, sustainable investments account for more than 10% of the Investment Portfolio. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships last November with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia through co-investment. Moreover, we issued the inaugural "HKMA ESG Expectations" document last September to further encourage fund managers to proactively exercise asset ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Access to financing is crucial for accelerating the regional transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred venue for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers—including provincial and municipal governments from the Mainland—Hong Kong plays a vital role in channelling capital to expedite the region's transition. The Action Plan sets out a vision to develop Hong Kong into the region’s premier sustainable finance platform and outlines objectives to foster innovation in sustainable finance. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme to drive green bond innovation—including the issuance of the world’s first multi-currency digital bonds last February—to expanding the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to cover transition finance instruments last May, and launching the Digital Bond Grant Scheme last November, we have consistently encouraged regional issuers to utilize Hong Kong’s financial platform to raise funds needed for decarbonization and transition. Achieving a robust transition requires not only capital and innovation but also an inclusive and accessible sustainability ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent disclosures, and professionals equipped with relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, the Action Plan commits us to supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures and addressing gaps in sustainable finance talent and expertise within the region. We have made good progress in assisting stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosures, particularly by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to support SMEs. Last November, we also launched a Professional-level module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking professionals to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. Furthermore, through events such as the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held last February, we have engaged diverse stakeholders in discussions on sustainable development to foster collaboration and innovation. Internally, the HKMA is committed to ensuring our operations align with our sustainability vision. Under the Action Plan, we have pledged to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or sooner, bringing forward our original target by 20 years. Additionally, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the Government’s roadmap. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low-carbon emissions as a selection criterion in our procurement processes. Meanwhile, we continue to enhance operational efficiency through digitalization, cultivate a culture of sustainability within the organization, and motivate staff to actively participate in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has long been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, yet the reshaping of the international order and dramatic shifts in geopolitics have introduced uncertainties to global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an undeniable reality that is steadily worsening. There is no room for complacency in our efforts to combat it. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong’s financial system while creating opportunities along the way. As we enter 2025, we will press ahead with determination, striving to advance our sustainability agenda and deepen ties with like-minded partners. Despite formidable challenges, we remain steadfast in our commitment to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is a defining challenge of our generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across the region and beyond. In October 2024, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), which sets out the HKMA’s vision in this area, including our future direction, timelines for achieving various objectives, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance these efforts. Through formulating strategic policies, strengthening supervisory engagement, and enhancing internal operations, the HKMA aims to strengthen the resilience of both the Hong Kong banking sector and the HKMA itself against climate-related risks, and to facilitate Asia's transition towards a more sustainable economy. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also seeks to exert influence and contribute to the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the banking sector’s climate resilience and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during their transition to net-zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - Launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks’ climate risk management practices and conducting a third round of consultative meetings to assess banks’ implementation of relevant HKMA supervisory requirements and to further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; - Refining the incorporation of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA’s supervisor-led stress testing framework; - Continuing to advance the integration of climate factors into the HKMA’s Supervisory Review Process; - Commencing preparatory work for developing relevant supervisory requirements regarding the implementation by the local banking sector of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks and the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - Finalising the new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. Beyond its role as a banking regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, striving to promote the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We have launched Phase 1 of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitating related capital flows. The HKMA has commenced work on Phase 2 of the Taxonomy to expand its coverage, including incorporating transition elements, adding green economic activities, and integrating climate adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another green fintech event in 2025 to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks. Hong Kong is well-positioned to support the region's sustainable financing needs. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme", whose expanded scope now covers sustainable projects such as social projects. This initiative will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a demonstration effect for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide funding through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to utilise Hong Kong’s financing platform for raising sustainable capital. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises from the Mainland and elsewhere to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing grants to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme". Despite growing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures from institutions and corporates, entities vary in their capacity and readiness to make such disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In light of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For instance, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with a richer set of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore ways to leverage technology to make existing resources more accessible; and partner with key local industry associations to deliver training tailored to the industry's needs. The sustainable finance landscape is evolving rapidly, necessitating an expansion of the local talent pool and bridging knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the wider region. Key initiatives for the HKMA in 2025 include collaborating with the banking sector to develop professional-level training modules under the "Green and Sustainable Finance" stream of the "Enhanced Competency Framework", and identifying areas where further training is needed through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026–2030" study. Additionally, we plan to work with key stakeholders to enhance promotion of the Government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" and review its scope of application. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks to launch dedicated programmes in Asia. These include conducting green finance research, providing unique market insights, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, fostering community engagement, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps for integrating green finance into their core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or sooner, in support of the broader economic transition. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that foster positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to leading by example in institutional sustainability. In line with the accelerated timeline for achieving net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Plan", the HKMA will progressively integrate environmental and social considerations into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting at a pragmatic pace, continuing to drive institutional sustainability. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to better understand the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring our focus remains on material topics. Furthermore, we will conduct energy audits and leverage technological solutions to assess the material impact of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government’s launch of the "Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap" and are actively undertaking preparatory work to make disclosures in accordance with ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will uphold its commitment to energy efficiency and conservation principles when selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to facilitate paperless processes and waste reduction, and improving the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable organization, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the wider Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of related initiatives; and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations and practices. In pursuit of sound institutional governance, the HKMA has put in place a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and establishes effective mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability efforts.
