The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability-related work, and provide recommendations; - The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides leadership at the management level on the HKMA’s overall Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) strategy and policy; - On responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - For other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability-related measures covering banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (CASG), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux and departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s various sustainability initiatives over recent years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability-related work across different functional areas of the HKMA. The Steering Committee: - Provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans relating to ESG matters across four functional areas: banking, the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; - Oversees the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by various functional departments of the HKMA; - Assesses the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - Oversees external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. In addition, Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainability matters are invited to attend meetings of the Steering Committee to report on key achievements and future plans regarding their respective work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups from the Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office of the HKMA. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA co-initiated the CASG with the SFC in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the CASG provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the CASG, please refer to the chapter entitled "Strengthening the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change poses risks to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to strengthening the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system against climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily business operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play a vital role in the financial system by channelling capital towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA launched the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), setting out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and to support sustainable development in Asia and beyond. The Action Plan comprises eight goals across four key areas. To assist the industry in achieving the relevant banking policy objectives, we have been undertaking the following initiatives. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or sooner, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or sooner. All banks are enhancing transparency regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2 "Transition Planning". This new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capabilities in managing the net-zero transition and related risk management. Furthermore, we are reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine Pillar 2 capital requirements. The objective is to incorporate relevant factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks, including transition planning, to address climate risks. The HKMA has been working to align local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) Standards and the Basel Committee’s Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is pivotal to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and to help channel capital towards green and sustainable activities. Covering 12 economic activities under four sectors, the Taxonomy aims to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating relevant elements tailored to local circumstances. We have commenced Phase 2 work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable capital. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and supported banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to address climate change. The HKMA also completed all tasks under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to integrate climate risk into the bank supervisory process. To enhance banks' capacity to manage climate risks, the HKMA shared good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultative meetings with the banking sector, which mainly include: - Establishing a robust governance structure with clearly defined responsibilities for the Board and senior management; - Ensuring effective oversight of key aspects of climate-related risk matters, including: (1) facilitating and overseeing the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategy; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a strong climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA organised a Balanced Supervision Roundtable focusing on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including challenges faced by banks in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and sustainable finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and supported the HKMA’s work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA conducted a round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held a second series of consultative meetings to assess the progress of a new cohort of banks in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" and to understand the challenges they face. The meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to individual banks to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), with participation from 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results indicated that under various scenarios, including those assuming concurrent climate risks and macroeconomic downturns, the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared to the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks have significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report detailing the CRST results and good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. Recognising the numerous data and methodology challenges banks face in climate risk management, the HKMA has been actively promoting the application of technology to address these issues. To tackle the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched the Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform based on user feedback and by incorporating more local data. Additionally, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the wider financial services sector. During the year, we published practical guides and two Regtech Adoption Case Briefs (in English), outlining technological solutions for Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also hosted the third "FiNETech", bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology firms to explore collaboration in green fintech. Acknowledging that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to enhance current surveillance efforts. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in various Financial Stability Reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA contributes to enriching climate scenarios, helping central banks and supervisors understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS released the fifth vintage of long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s Transition Planning Working Group, the HKMA participates in analysing the interplay between transition planning in financial and non-financial corporates and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the "Practical Guide on Green Technology Adoption for Banks" (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA has undertaken several applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. Research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in mitigating monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition to a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only deepen our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding policy formulation. Locally, this research supports the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. Research findings are also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels such as HKMA Research Memoranda. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research, the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission firms benefit significantly from carbon pricing and highlights its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the Institute’s "Insights from Monetary Research" and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA’s Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through this engagement, we contribute to policy dialogues on tackling climate change and its implications for financial stability at both international and regional levels, drawing on insights gained to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading regional green and sustainable finance hub, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA’s “Sustainable Finance Action Plan” (“Action Plan”), the HKMA is dedicated to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we strive to establish Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and beyond, support technological innovation in the green segment of the financial market, enhance sustainable disclosure by the industry, expand the local green talent pool, and address knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Establishing Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and beyond Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure Bridging talent and knowledge gaps in regional sustainable finance To demonstrate the Government’s commitment to tackling climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the “Government Green Bond Programme” in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing a total of approximately US$28 billion equivalent in green bonds to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, covering areas such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private sector green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the programme and further consolidate Hong Kong’s status as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects, and it was renamed the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme” (GSBP). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the GSBP, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$3 billion equivalent of institutional green bonds under the GSBP. This triple-tranche issuance covered bonds of different tenors denominated in Renminbi, US dollars, and Euros. These bonds attracted participation from diverse categories of investors and were met with strong subscription, recording over US$15 billion equivalent in orders. Notably, the 20-year and 30-year Renminbi green bonds marked the Government’s first issuance of such tenors, representing the longest-dated Renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date. They provide new benchmarks for the market and further demonstrate the catalytic role of the GSBP. These bonds also further enrich the choice of offshore Renminbi investment products in Hong Kong. Moreover, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government’s green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong’s dedication to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more regional borrowers to utilise Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise funds for sustainable development, the HKMA continues to implement the “Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme” launched in May 2021, which provides grants to eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well received by the industry. As at end-2024, grants had been approved for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value exceeding US$140 billion. The scheme was extended in May 2024 for three years until 2027, with its coverage expanded to include transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to utilise Hong Kong’s transition finance platform for gradual decarbonisation. - Grants approved for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value exceeding US$140 billion (as at end-2024) - Extended for three years until 2027, with coverage expanded to include transition finance instruments Meanwhile, the HKMA has actively promoted Hong Kong’s sustainable financing platform, achieving positive results. Notably, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government made its fourth issuance of offshore municipal government bonds in Hong Kong in August, totalling RMB 7 billion, comprising RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 900 million in social bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People’s Government made its inaugural issuance of offshore bonds in Hong Kong, totalling RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial People’s Government also made its third issuance of offshore bonds in Hong Kong, totalling RMB 3 billion, including RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuances have repeatedly underscored Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. With these various measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the premier platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained the largest hub for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances in Asia in 2024, with related bonds arranged through Hong Kong totalling US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tranches of tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the world’s first tokenised government green bonds and the world’s first multi-currency digital bonds. These issuances demonstrate the Government’s support for market participants in the region to apply asset digitisation and innovative technologies in the green and sustainable finance space. The HKMA also launched the “Digital Bond Grant Scheme” in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in the local green and sustainable finance market. The Working Group on Sustainability Disclosure under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (CASG) has been working on the adoption of the “International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards” (ISSB Standards) in Hong Kong. The Government released the “Hong Kong Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure” in December 2024, providing a clear pathway for large Public Interest Entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of readiness in achieving high-quality sustainability disclosure, making sustainability disclosure more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the use of the “Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies” (Questionnaire), launched by the CASG in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides user-friendly disclosure templates to facilitate sustainability disclosure by companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to enable online completion by companies (see QR code below). The HKMA is refining the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and latest international developments to make it more user-friendly. Specific measures include identifying core questions within the Questionnaire and providing common usage scenarios. In addition, we are striving to enhance the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools available on the CASG website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. Leading by example, the HKMA demonstrates its commitment by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards. The report contains rich content on the HKMA’s climate-related operational risks, as well as plans and implementation progress towards achieving climate targets. For details on sustainability disclosures regarding our own operations, please refer to the chapter “A Sustainable HKMA”. Given the rapidly evolving landscape of the sustainable finance market, the HKMA is strengthening skills training for the banking sector and facilitating knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to bridge knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, in conjunction with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the Foundation Level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework in July 2023. This module aims to help professionals in the banking sector acquire knowledge in green and sustainable finance more effectively and develop relevant professional competencies. It covers four key functional areas: (1) Green and Sustainable Finance Products and Services; (2) Sustainability/Climate Risk Management; (3) Sustainability Disclosure and Reporting; and (4) Sustainability Strategy, Compliance, and Controls. Furthermore, the Professional Level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, targeting mid-to-senior level banking practitioners responsible for relevant functions, was also launched in November. To provide necessary training for banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the administering body of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, launched the training programme for the Foundation Level in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking sector in 2025 to develop the training programme for the Professional Level. To understand the further skills and training needs of the banking sector, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking sector on the “Future Banking Talent 2026–2030” study, with the aim of publishing the findings in 2025. This joint study follows up on the “Future Banking Talent 2021–2025” paper published in June 2020. The findings of this follow-up study will serve as an important reference for the industry to formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. Through collaboration with the CASG, the HKMA also continues to assist in implementing the Government-funded “Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme”, which subsidises practitioners, graduates, and students to receive sustainable finance-related training. As at December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses had been registered as eligible training courses under the scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025-26 Budget that the scheme will be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the Coalition for Sustainable Investing Capacity Building (CASI), the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative instruments. In addition, the HKMA supported the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in establishing a chapter in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ’s network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) plays an active leading role in promoting green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund. It prioritises sustainable assets and requires its external investment managers to exercise active ownership. Guided by the principle of "Capital Preservation First, Long-term Growth Second," the HKMA invests prudently, believing that adequate attention to Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate relevant investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieve better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Chart 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made this document available to investment partners through annual ESG workshops and the HKMA website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organisations to develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment practices within the financial sector and central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we strive to foster a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), articulating its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or sooner, and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, thereby further solidifying its dedication to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC), chaired by the Financial Secretary, has established the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to balance responsible investment practices with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee, under the EFAC and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors implementation progress through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the EFIO. As shown in Chart 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and oversees various ESG initiatives within the EFIO. Motions and work progress discussed at quarterly meetings of the ESG Committee are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the EFIO. Furthermore, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the EFIO, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the EFIO, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG goals. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the EFIO on integrating ESG factors, and assists senior management in managing ESG risks and opportunities—particularly those related to climate change—across different investment portfolios: - Public Market Investments: The Credit, Compliance and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior management of the EFIO, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models based on input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of fixed income portfolios through regular reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Division. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios from an ESG perspective (for details, refer to the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 39). - Private Market Investments: The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private markets investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal. The HKMA recognises that physical and transition risks arising from climate change, along with associated opportunities, will affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund's investments. The United Nations Environment Programme's "Emissions Gap Report 2024" projects that unless there is massive and rapid global mobilisation to cut greenhouse gas emissions, global average temperatures will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties regarding policy changes, technological developments, and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amidst these challenges, as governments and industries turn towards sustainable solutions, investment opportunities with potentially attractive long-term prospects are emerging in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. Believing that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, the HKMA places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner, and continues to advance this goal through an orderly three-pronged approach (see Chart 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the "Action Plan," which reinforces the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Chart 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusion or divestment from investable assets. Investing in a Sustainable Future Achieving Net-Zero Emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or Sooner - Actively expanding the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with special focus on climate change and transition outlook considerations - Formulating clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, requiring compliance from all external investment managers, investee companies, and counterparties - Committed to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from 2017 levels by 2030 Supporting Regional Transition Through Investment - Continuing engagement with external investment managers to optimise transition-driving investment opportunities - Continuing to identify and prioritise high-quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia's transition and generate positive global impact First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objectives. Direct exclusion of certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risk profiles. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition—including those in high-emission sectors—that possess superior technology and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not solve carbon emission problems. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and exercising active ownership, driving their transition towards sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about beneficial changes for both the industries themselves and the world at large. Net-zero investment approaches have evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, driving economy-wide decarbonisation. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of its portfolio relies not only on internal adjustments but also on broad-based economic transition. While there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting both the Exchange Fund's and global net-zero goals. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilting, and thematic investing across various asset classes aligned with net-zero pathways. In public markets, this may involve tilting portfolios towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, complemented by stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, greater emphasis may be placed on transition-facilitating investments. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continuously identifies investment opportunities that promote climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio," with financial performance comparable to relevant portfolio benchmarks (Chart 5). - Public Market Investments: The HKMA launched an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek Green, Social and Sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see the section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds" for relevant case studies). - Private Market Investments: The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA actively sources and evaluates investment opportunities that accelerate energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see the section "Joining Forces to Tackle Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond" for examples). - Passive portfolios benchmarked against ESG indices - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios with non-ESG benchmarks - Active portfolios with a governance theme - Active ESG portfolios focused on sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed around energy transition and decarbonisation globally, in Asia, and in the Global South - Green, Social and Sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" initiative, offering Paris Agreement-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a quasi-governmental entity. Proceeds raised from the green bonds were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading aging equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades cover optimising monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits through wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continuous wastewater and sludge treatment, these facilities compost or reuse dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement, and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. The facilities also utilise gas generated during sludge treatment to fuel boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. The bonds finance multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess water from rivers to arid regions. The project primarily aims to rehabilitate deteriorating canal linings to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged areas. Additionally, the project provides skills training for local stakeholders, promoting the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation techniques such as micro-irrigation and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organization. A key focus of the HKMA’s efforts in 2024 to fulfill this commitment was the plan to advance the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its own operations to 2030, bringing forward the original target by 20 years, in line with the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan". In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and well-being, promoting financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the primary decision-making body for various organizational sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions in its operations by 2030 or earlier, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures related to corporate operations, staff well-being, and community engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on the organization's sustainability initiatives. Additional support is provided by the Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Team, both composed of staff from various operational departments; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing ideas on creating a green workplace, while the latter aims to foster a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA’s dedication to caring for the environment, its staff, and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years+ Caring Organization" logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA’s sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: Environment, People, and Social Responsibility. - Focusing on decarbonization and digitalization of the HKMA’s daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier - Adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promoting greener practices to the financial sector and the wider community - Building a motivated workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA’s strategic objectives - Creating a collaborative, caring, and inclusive work environment that values diversity and enhances staff sense of belonging - Providing a quality work environment that promotes healthy lifestyles - Fostering a culture of social responsibility - Integrating social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promoting financial inclusion and enhancing public financial literacy through consumer education initiatives The HKMA is concerned about climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, as part of the "Action Plan", the HKMA announced plans to advance the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its own operations to 2030, bringing forward its previous commitment by 20 years. The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations, with an emphasis on reducing carbon emissions, conserving energy and paper, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix of local power companies for electricity generation. Furthermore, the HKMA has established a digitalized workplace to enhance efficiency while simultaneously reducing its carbon footprint. Recognizing the importance of cultivating a sustainability culture, the HKMA encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programs and events. Under the overarching 2030 net-zero emissions target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and making low-carbon procurement choices wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel by purchasing Sustainable Aviation Fuel and participating in carbon offset projects. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting schemes to cover all remaining major sources of carbon emissions. Beyond the above-mentioned environmental commitments regarding its physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the low-carbon transition of the market, ranging from introducing electronic submission and processing procedures to promoting e-payments and facilitating the recirculation of coins. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA’s strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as promoting staff well-being and social responsibility. Under the HKMA’s overall Enterprise Risk Management Framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing and reviewing potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To better assess the potential impact of climate change on its operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the HKMA’s offices are designed with multiple measures incorporated to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire, and other emergencies. Additionally, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures covering not only office premises but also telecommunications and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation drills and backup facility activation exercises to ensure staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA also monitors its exposure to transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage resulting from its own operations. The HKMA’s latest climate targets are to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions associated with its organizational operations by 2030 or earlier. These targets were developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology. The HKMA adopts the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its organizational emissions. Scope 1 emissions arise from direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA’s primary greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect emissions resulting from the consumption of fossil fuels for electricity generation. Due to the lack of supplier-specific data, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate material Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills, as well as staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are presented in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. Performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria of the verification are set out in the accompanying "Verification Statement" at the end of this report. The HKMA practices what it preaches, adhering to the same climate-related standards expected of the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this initiative in 2025 to achieve full green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into office design, operations, and maintenance. Specifically, during various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting-out materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To improve overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in its offices and data centers. In the 2024 Data Center Facility Upgrade Project, the HKMA adopted a modular Uninterruptible Power Supply system to further optimize the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus certified data center. This design allows for flexible capacity scaling, improved operational efficiency under partial loads, and features advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. Through its Digital Workplace, the HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration and streamlines workflows, effectively reducing paper consumption. Moreover, referencing manufacturers' software update cycles, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices, thereby prolonging their secure usage period. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the "4R" principles—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are placed at convenient locations throughout the office. To increase recycling rates, the HKMA added collection bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit mesh bags in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a Waste-to-Energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Charter", pledging to take measures to reduce waste generated from various events. The HKMA continues to prioritize the procurement of products meeting the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan trips carefully, such as combining multiple journeys when attending overseas events. At the organizational level, since 2023, the HKMA has purchased Sustainable Aviation Fuel, reducing annual air travel carbon emissions by approximately 10%. Additionally, the HKMA participates in Gold Standard certified carbon offset projects to offset the remaining air travel emissions; these projects focus on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA organized various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of Waste-to-Energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on April 22, 2024, throughout the month of May, the HKMA held its inaugural "HKMA Green Month" under the theme "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This served as an excellent opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment and momentum in practicing environmental sustainability in its internal operations. Activities included the "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" encouraging staff to practice green living, the "Save the Earth" quiz, and a Japanese-inspired "Kokedama" indoor plant workshop; waste audit findings were shared, and operators of community recycling centers introduced best practices in recycling. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month", the HKMA launched a six-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that collective small changes in habits can significantly improve the organization's overall recycling performance. A highlight of the campaign was the launch of the "Green 'Fit' Action" video series, featuring senior executives sharing recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and e-alerts to remind staff to practice waste reduction and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability and gather feedback on proposed green office measures. The survey results will assist in formulating future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as a key enabler of change and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable practices across the financial sector and the wider community. The HKMA has introduced various measures to enhance the efficiency of external-facing processes. Following the successful launch of the "Common Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's coverage in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as Stored Value Facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The expansion aims to further streamline submission processes for reporting entities, provide a smoother user experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA’s commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 include SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA surveys via simplified submission processes, and the Intelligent Information and Document Management System, a centralized platform providing users with advanced search and bank-related document functions.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste disposed of at landfills and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel for 2024, as well as their respective intensities. In addition, the Data includes Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions arising from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste disposed of at landfills and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, along with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data has been prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol"), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers a total of six office and warehouse assets, comprising five offices located at: 1) Two International Finance Centre; 2) Hopewell Centre; 3) One Pacific Place; 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre; and 5) Global Trade Square; and one warehouse located at 6) Lok Sing Industrial Building, Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the six assets. This verification engagement was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to obtain a reasonable level of assurance for forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was carried out in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to its sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, as well as conducting reliability testing. The verification process also included validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work was conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - The Data is materially accurate and reliable; and - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shen Xiaoyin Audit Manager Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
